coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help ReGLOSS award the tournament's most memorable achievements without starting another competition.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Ririka has sponsorship envelopes. Hajime has a strict seating plan. Kanade has a microphone set to a volume labeled DO NOT. Raden has prepared historical context for each award. The trophy table includes categories such as BEST RESCUE, BEST COLLISION, and MOST LEGALLY INTERESTING SHORTCUT.

steps.prompt: Ririka asks which category should open the ceremony. Hajime warns that the winners are already arguing backstage.

options.resultDialogue: Kanade announces every team that touched the falling banner. Six groups walk onstage. Hajime counts them. 'There is one trophy.' Ririka whispers, 'I can sell five runner-up trophies.' Raden says, 'You had them prepared.' Ririka says nothing, which is an answer.

The nominees include Subaru versus Korone, Pekora versus foam, and HoloTori versus the concept of landing. Subaru raises a hand. 'Why am I nominated twice?' Kanade checks the card. 'Consistency!' Subaru lowers her hand and begins reconsidering sports.

options.text: Open with Most Creative Rule Use
options.resultDialogue: Fubuki, Miko, Pekora, and Okayu all step forward before their names are called. Hajime stares at them. 'This is not evidence in your favor.' Raden begins explaining the historical difference between interpretation and evasion. Pekora asks whether the lecture has a fast lane.

steps.prompt: A four-way argument begins over the People's Choice trophy. Ririka asks the Manager to resolve it before Kanade turns the dispute into a chant.

options.resultDialogue: Kanade measures applause with the microphone. Polka conducts one side of the audience, Korone flexes at another, and Kiara starts a HoloTori chant. The meter overloads and displays EVERYONE. Hajime points at the screen. 'Democracy has failed.' Ririka replies, 'Democracy has upsold.'

Hajime creates separate awards for athletic skill, audience impact, rescue work, and accidental infrastructure. Everyone receives exactly one category except Pekora, whose category reads UNDER REVIEW. Pekora holds it proudly. 'Exclusive-peko.'

Raden explains that history remembers events, not placements. Miko raises her hand. 'So the crater wins?' Raden pauses. Polka stands beside the crater trophy. 'The scholar has spoken.' Raden closes her notes. 'I regret leaving room for interpretation.'

steps.prompt: The unofficial ceremony needs one final award that can end the night without causing a rematch.

options.resultDialogue: Ririka presents one enormous certificate to every staff member, competitor, medic, repair crew, and unwilling Flock Commander. Subaru checks her copy. 'Why does mine still say bird division?' Kiara hugs her before she can file another appeal. Kanade shouts, 'EVERYONE WINS!' Hajime quietly locks the arena gates.
options.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS concluded the People's Choice Awards by honoring everyone who kept the Summer Games operating. The ceremony ended before anyone could challenge the certificate to a rematch.

options.resultDialogue: The nominees are the parade flight, Miko's cart, the banner rescue, and Pekora's shortcut economy. The audience votes for ALL OF THE ABOVE. Ririka unveils a trophy shaped like a repair invoice. Pekora asks whether it is tax-deductible. Hajime escorts her away from the microphone.
options.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS awarded the tournament's collective disasters with a trophy shaped like an invoice. The resort accepted the joke and kept the actual invoices.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS completed the unofficial awards ceremony. No findings occurred, and every category has been closed to appeals until management recovers.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Sora and AZKi give the exhausted resort a calm encore while the lighthouse remains under observation.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Sora has chosen an acoustic set. AZKi is monitoring the sound system for the prism's frequency even though the prism is secured elsewhere. The audience is tired, the competitors are bandaged, and Korone has been asked not to challenge the speakers.

steps.prompt: Sora asks what atmosphere the resort needs after the tournament. AZKi checks a waveform and says, 'Preferably one without an infrastructure response.'

options.resultDialogue: Sora begins a soft song. Conversations fade, ice packs stop rustling, and even Pekora lowers her voice to a whisper. 'This is suspiciously peaceful-peko.' Marine whispers back, 'Senchou believes we should sell the silence.' Flare turns around. Both stop talking.

Subaru requests something energetic, Okayu requests something sleepy, and Miko requests an elite anthem with explosions. AZKi creates one arrangement that begins fast, slows into a lullaby, and ends before Miko's explosion cue. Miko waits beside the button. Nothing happens. 'The song betrayed me-nye.'

options.text: Perform the Summer Games theme quietly
options.resultDialogue: AZKi strips the theme down to piano and voice. The audience recognizes the melody and begins swaying. Polka lifts a confetti cannon. Flare lowers it without looking away from the stage. Polka whispers, 'She has developed peripheral management.'

steps.prompt: Halfway through the concert, the speakers reproduce a faint mechanical note matching the lighthouse signal from Day 7.

options.resultDialogue: AZKi lowers the music and separates the signal. It repeats once, then stops. 'Same frequency,' she says. Sora looks toward the dark lighthouse. 'But the prism is not here.' A staff member asks whether the audience noticed. Behind them, everyone is waving glowsticks perfectly in time with the tone.

options.text: Blend the tone into the song
options.resultDialogue: Sora matches the note gently while AZKi harmonizes around it. The lighthouse remains dark, but the ocean surface ripples in one straight line toward the missing pier's coordinates. The audience assumes it is part of the stage lighting. There is no stage lighting on the water.

options.text: Stop the speakers and continue unplugged
options.resultDialogue: AZKi disconnects the system. Sora continues without amplification, and the entire crowd becomes quiet enough to hear the waves. The mechanical tone does not return. Korone leans toward Okayu. 'Did we defeat it?' Okayu whispers, 'By unplugging it.' Korone nods with deep respect for technology.

steps.prompt: The concert reaches its final song. Sora asks whether to end with a message to the guests or quietly close the night.

options.resultDialogue: Sora thanks the competitors, repair crews, medics, referees, and guests. AZKi adds, 'Tomorrow can be quieter.' From the back, Pekora asks, 'How much quieter?' Flare answers, 'You are not invited to test the limit.' The audience laughs, and the lights fade normally.
options.completionDialogue: SorAZ closed the aftermath day with a calm thank-you concert. A faint lighthouse tone returned briefly, but the night ended without another projection or artifact.

options.text: End with a silent final bow
options.resultDialogue: Sora and AZKi finish the final chord and bow without speaking. The audience follows, quiet for one full second. Then Kanade shouts 'ENCORE!' from somewhere outside the venue. Hajime's voice follows: 'NO.' The applause resumes anyway.
options.completionDialogue: SorAZ ended the night with a silent bow and no further lighthouse response. The resort achieved one full second of peace before Kanade requested an encore.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: SorAZ completed the quiet encore. No finding occurred; the only anomaly was a brief repetition of the known lighthouse signal.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Justice organize the fourth pier evidence before Gigi arrests the ocean.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Elizabeth has opened a formal case titled THE NONEXISTENT PIER. Cecilia has three data displays. Raora has pinned sketches across the wall. Gigi is wearing a life jacket and carrying handcuffs. 'If the pier is hiding in the ocean, the ocean is an accomplice.'

steps.prompt: Justice must choose the strongest evidence for the official file. Elizabeth refuses to list 'Gigi feels suspicious' as a technical source.

options.resultDialogue: Cecilia projects the coordinates over the current resort map. They point to open water. Gigi circles the location twelve times. Elizabeth asks why. 'Tactical emphasis.' Raora draws a tiny pier inside the circles. Cecilia says, 'The drawing is not measurement data.' Raora adds a ruler.

Elizabeth places the old UNIT-Z badge record beside the lighthouse data. Cecilia confirms both use the same obsolete serial format. Gigi points at the page. 'So Z built the pier.' Elizabeth says, 'That is not what the letter means.' Gigi writes Z DID IT in the margin anyway.

Cecilia displays CALIBRATION ONE OF FOUR COMPLETE. Elizabeth underlines ONE OF FOUR. Raora draws four empty boxes. Gigi fills the first with a bird. Elizabeth erases it. Gigi draws a smaller bird. Cecilia concludes, 'The island expects three additional calibration events.' Everyone stops joking for almost two seconds.

Raora displays sketches from the crowd. Every drawing shows the pier differently: ancient, futuristic, covered in birds, or shaped like Korone. Elizabeth chooses the least artistic version. Raora looks wounded. 'That one has no atmosphere.' Cecilia replies, 'It has scale markings.'

steps.prompt: Guests are asking whether the fourth pier was part of the Summer Games finale. Justice needs a public position.

options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth issues a temporary maritime restriction. Gigi runs outside with warning tape. Cecilia watches through the window. 'She cannot tape the ocean.' Raora says, 'She has already taped two waves.' Elizabeth closes her eyes. 'Add environmental cleanup to the order.'

options.text: Call it an unplanned visual effect
options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth delivers the statement with perfect authority. A reporter asks who designed the effect. Everyone looks at Raora. Raora points at Cecilia. Cecilia points at the lighthouse. Gigi points at the ocean. The reporter writes COLLABORATIVE INSTALLATION.

Raora removes the unknown symbols, Gigi's suspect arrows, and Elizabeth's legal notes. The final image shows only the outline of the pier. Guests immediately begin drawing theories around it. Raora watches the fan art multiply. 'We removed the speculation.' Cecilia replies, 'We provided a template.'

steps.prompt: The prism remains secured in the resort vault. Justice must choose the next official action without beginning an unsafe nighttime expedition.

options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth approves a daylight survey for a later date. Cecilia begins equipment requirements. Raora volunteers to document it. Gigi raises both hands. 'I volunteer to tackle the pier.' Elizabeth writes NO TACKLING INFRASTRUCTURE as the first rule.
options.completionDialogue: Justice scheduled a controlled future survey of the fourth pier coordinates. The prism remains secured, and no one is permitted to tackle the destination.

options.text: Lock the case until new evidence appears
options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth seals the file. Cecilia encrypts the data. Raora stores the sketches. Gigi places handcuffs around the filing cabinet handles. 'Now the case cannot escape.' Elizabeth tests the cabinet. It is genuinely locked. 'Give me the key.' Gigi looks toward the ocean. 'The pier has it.'
options.completionDialogue: Justice sealed the fourth pier case pending new evidence. The documents are secure, although Gigi has misplaced the filing cabinet key in the name of operational realism.

options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth authorizes observation shifts from the lighthouse. Cecilia installs sensors. Raora designs a watch log. Gigi appears in a captain's hat and points at the water. 'Ocean, you are under surveillance.' Elizabeth removes the hat. 'You are not in command.' Gigi produces a second hat.
options.completionDialogue: Justice established a non-invasive maritime watch over the missing pier's coordinates. The first watch report contains useful sensor data and seventeen drawings of suspicious waves.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Justice organized the known fourth pier evidence without discovering a new object or entering the water. The case remains open, documented, and heavily annotated by Gigi.

days.storyBeat: Small management decisions begin producing strangely literal results around the resort. The guests treat every impossible rule, moving stage, silent hotel, and vending-machine boss fight as part of the entertainment, while a few systems quietly begin using the phrase 'Management Precedent.'

morning.title: Day 9 — Manager Said So
morning.openingDialogue: The resort opens normally for approximately four minutes. Then a temporary welcome rule becomes enforceable, a timetable starts arguing with time, and holoX discovers that spoken authority can move elevators. Nobody has yet agreed that these events are related.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Gen 1 write one harmless welcome rule. The resort appears to have a very broad definition of 'harmless.'
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Matsuri has been asked to write a one-line welcome rule for today's beach fair. Aki has the guest map, Mel is checking the entrance ribbons, and Haachama is holding a marker that management should probably confiscate.

steps.prompt: The signboard asks for one temporary fair rule. Matsuri grins. 'Manager, we have been trusted with legislation.' What do you approve?

options.resultDialogue: Matsuri writes EVERY GUEST MUST SAY WASSHOI. The turnstile immediately refuses to open for a silent tourist. Matsuri stares at it, then at you. 'Manager... the gate respects culture.' Aki tests it with a polite hello. Red light. Matsuri whispers, 'Say the sacred word.'

Haachama writes ALL OUTSIDE FOOD MUST PASS HAACHAMA INSPECTION. Every vending machine shutters at once. Mel reads the sign twice. 'That sounds like a health regulation written by the health violation.' Haachama puts on disposable gloves. 'Exactly!'

Aki draws three simple dance steps beside the gate. The moving walkway immediately begins matching the rhythm. Matsuri hops on and is carried sideways in perfect tempo. 'THIS IS AMAZING!' Mel grabs the rail. 'This is infrastructure choreography.'

steps.prompt: The rule is no longer decorative; resort equipment is enforcing it. How do you keep the fair moving?

options.resultDialogue: You add the word OPTIONAL. The turnstile, vending machines, and walkway all stop their nonsense at the same instant. Matsuri looks offended. 'The island has no appreciation for commitment.' Haachama quietly tries to erase OPTIONAL. Mel takes the marker away without looking.

You declare the rule part of the attraction. Guests start lining up to trigger it on purpose. Aki's dance lane becomes a photo spot, Matsuri judges Wasshoi volume, and Haachama starts stamping snack passports. Mel watches the queue double. 'I hate that this is successful.'

steps.prompt: The fair is running, but the signboard asks whether today's rule should be saved as a resort precedent.

options.resultDialogue: You press DELETE. The signboard flashes ARE YOU SURE? Matsuri presses NO before you can move. You press YES. She presses NO. This continues until Mel gently unplugs the sign. 'Democracy has ended.'
options.completionDialogue: Gen 1's beach fair opened normally after management wrestled a signboard for legislative control. The rule is gone, although Matsuri has kept a handwritten copy titled Constitution 2.

options.resultDialogue: You approve a special-event version. The signboard prints a gold certificate reading MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED. Everyone goes quiet for half a second. Haachama points at it. 'Can I frame that in the kitchen?' You tear the certificate in half. The printer makes another.
options.completionDialogue: The beach fair ended successfully, and one absurd temporary rule now exists as an official special-event policy. Nobody can explain why the printer was so eager to preserve it.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Gen 1 completed the beach fair. The guests had fun, the rules became alarmingly enforceable, and management has stopped letting Matsuri stand near legal-size paper.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Promise keep the resort exactly on time after Kronii makes the mistake of asking reality to cooperate.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Kronii is staring at a timetable with the expression of someone personally betrayed by minutes. Bae is shaking a cup full of numbered schedule tokens, Fauna has brought tea for the delayed guests, and IRyS keeps saying, 'I'm sure it'll work out,' which Kronii considers hostile.

steps.prompt: Three tours are running late. Kronii asks for one management directive to stabilize the schedule.

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'No delays today.' Every clock in the lobby stops. Kronii slowly looks up. 'Technically...' Bae screams, 'WE DEFEATED TIME!' Kronii grabs her by the shoulders. 'Do not celebrate my professional humiliation.'

Fauna adds a five-minute rest after every activity. The benches immediately slide into the walkways and refuse to move until someone sits down. Bae tries to vault one. A second bench intercepts her. Fauna smiles. 'Nature heals.' Bae, pinned between cushions, replies, 'Nature profiles me.'

options.text: Let Bae make the schedule flexible
options.resultDialogue: Bae writes MAYBE beside every start time. The departure board instantly changes to 10:00-ish, Lunch-adjacent, and When The Vibes Are Right. Kronii makes a sound no clock has ever made. IRyS pats her shoulder. 'Hope is flexible.' 'Hope is late.'

steps.prompt: Guests are enjoying the bizarre schedule more than the normal one. Kronii insists this is not evidence.

options.text: Force the clocks back to normal
options.resultDialogue: Kronii resets the master clock. Time resumes all at once. Every delayed chime rings simultaneously, Bae gets hit by twelve cuckoo noises, and IRyS applauds. Kronii smooths her hair. 'Perfect.' Fauna checks the lobby. 'A child thinks it's New Year's.'

You authorize a single five-minute grace period. The resort immediately labels it KRONII STANDARD TIME. Bae falls to the floor laughing. Kronii points at you with terrifying calm. 'Manager. Fix your island.' IRyS whispers, 'I think it likes you.'

steps.prompt: The timetable prints a final line: AUTHORITY CONFIRMED — MANAGER. What goes in today's report?

options.resultDialogue: Kronii circles MALFUNCTION three times. Bae adds 'fun malfunction.' Kronii crosses out 'fun.' Bae adds it back in glitter pen. Fauna quietly serves tea while the war over one adjective continues.
options.completionDialogue: Promise restored the day's schedule and filed the incident as a timing malfunction. The clocks work again, although one lobby display now judges every delay personally.

options.resultDialogue: IRyS copies AUTHORITY CONFIRMED — MANAGER into the report. Kronii stares at it. 'That is not how clocks work.' Bae points at the frozen clock behind her. 'Counterpoint.' Kronii turns the report face-down.
options.completionDialogue: Promise finished the schedule crisis and preserved one strange system message linking the resort's behavior directly to the Manager. Bae has titled the incident 'Manager vs. Time: Manager Won.'

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Promise kept the resort on schedule, more or less. Time itself was briefly involved in the labor dispute.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Give holoX temporary attraction-control access without allowing La+ to become the building.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: La+ has requested temporary administrator access for the guest attraction controls. Iroha has prepared a sensible permission list, Koyori has prepared a forty-page experiment proposal, and Chloe is asleep on the card reader.

steps.prompt: The control terminal asks which holoX member receives temporary authority.

options.resultDialogue: La+ slaps the badge onto her chest. 'AT LAST. THE RESORT ACKNOWLEDGES ITS RULER.' Every automatic door opens for her from twenty meters away. She points at Iroha. 'Bow.' The nearest elevator descends to Basement 1. Iroha watches the doors close. 'It appears the building misunderstood, de gozaru.'

Iroha receives the badge. Every door immediately begins asking other holoX members for identification. Koyori presents seven laminated science permits. The door rejects all seven. Chloe, still asleep, rolls through when it opens for Iroha. Koyori whispers, 'Favoritism.'

Koyori taps TEST ALL. The terminal grants her access to lights, music, shutters, fountains, and something labeled WEATHER MAYBE. Iroha reaches for the keyboard. Koyori hugs it. 'Science has seniority!' La+ points at the sky. 'GIVE ME THUNDER.' Iroha takes the keyboard faster.

steps.prompt: The building is treating spoken holoX orders as control commands. La+ notices first, which is unfortunate.

options.resultDialogue: Iroha says, 'Open the west gate.' It opens. La+ says, 'Open my path to domination.' Nothing happens. She tries again louder. Chloe wakes up just long enough to say, 'Skill issue,' then falls back asleep. La+ begins drafting treason charges.

La+ points dramatically. 'I WANT EVERYONE BENEATH ME!' Every elevator in the building drops to the basement. Silence. Koyori checks the panel. 'Technically, everyone is now beneath your office.' La+ crosses her arms. 'As intended.' Iroha: 'Please stop succeeding accidentally.'

steps.prompt: Iroha has control again. The terminal asks whether to remember today's voice-authority settings.

options.resultDialogue: Iroha clears the permissions. La+ gives one final command: 'REMEMBER YOUR TRUE MASTER!' The terminal replies USER NOT RECOGNIZED. Chloe wakes up to laugh once, very quietly, then returns to sleep.
options.completionDialogue: holoX returned the attraction controls to normal. La+ lost supreme building authority and has begun a personal feud with Door 3.

options.resultDialogue: You preserve voice control for emergencies. The terminal prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED. Koyori's ears perk up. 'Precedent?' La+ grabs the paper. 'Proof of my reign!' Iroha takes it back. 'Proof that Manager should choose words carefully.'
options.completionDialogue: holoX kept a restricted emergency voice-control system. The resort now has a documented habit of treating Manager-approved temporary rules as permanent enough to print certificates about.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoX finished the access test without taking over the resort. This is being counted as a success.

noon.title: Day 9 — Temporary Means Temporary
noon.openingDialogue: By noon, the island is treating jokes like paperwork. Volunteers become husbands, a doodled shortcut becomes architecture, and one hotel attempts to enforce silence as a physical law.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Staff a crowded lunch event after Nene solves the volunteer shortage through marriage.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Nene is recruiting helpers for the lunch rush. Lamy has clipboards, Botan has logistics maps, and the volunteer counter is stuck at twelve. Nene looks at the line of guests, then at you. 'Manager. I know how to increase family participation.'

steps.prompt: Nene proposes calling every volunteer a 'temporary husband' because her fans already use the title. How far do you let this go?

options.text: Use it as a cute nickname
options.resultDialogue: You approve the nickname. The badge printer immediately spits out twelve cards reading NENE HUSBAND — TEMPORARY STAFF. Lamy goes pale. 'Those look legally formatted.' Botan scans one. 'It has employee access.' Nene raises both arms. 'MARRIAGE HAS BENEFITS!'

You insist on VOLUNTEER. Nene writes HUSBAND underneath in pink marker. The printer rejects the correction, then prints SPOUSE (UNVERIFIED). Botan tilts her head. 'The machine compromised.' Lamy whispers, 'Why is the machine negotiating?'

Botan suggests AUXILIARY STAFF. Nene hears 'auxiliary husbands.' Five minutes later, the volunteers have squad numbers, matching aprons, and a chant. Lamy looks at Botan. Botan looks at Nene. 'I accept partial responsibility.'

steps.prompt: The new badges begin assigning real resort tasks—and real staff benefits.

options.resultDialogue: You let the system issue free staff lunches. Nene's volunteers cheer. Then the terminal adds FAMILY DISCOUNT: 100%. Lamy grabs the keyboard. 'How large does it think this family is?' Botan checks the counter. 'Increasing.' Nene is still recruiting.

You hit CANCEL ALL TEMPORARY RELATIONSHIPS. The printer asks REASON FOR DIVORCE. Nene gasps so loudly the lunch queue stops. 'MANAGER!' Botan takes a photo of your face. Lamy says, 'We can use 'seasonal staffing correction.'' The printer accepts it with suspicious sympathy.

steps.prompt: The lunch rush is solved. What do you do with the volunteer program?

options.text: Keep the squad, lose the marriage
options.resultDialogue: You reissue the badges as NENE SUPPORT CREW. Nene studies hers. 'Can they still call me wife?' Lamy says, 'Off the clock.' Botan adds, 'Not a payroll question.' The volunteers cheer anyway.
options.completionDialogue: NePoLaBo survived the lunch rush with a suspiciously devoted volunteer corps. Management has clarified that fandom terminology does not create legal spouses.

options.resultDialogue: You keep the joke title for special events. The terminal prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED: HUSBAND STAFFING MODEL. Lamy puts both hands over her face. Botan reads the projected labor savings. 'Manager, financially... this is annoyingly effective.' Nene starts planning uniforms.
options.completionDialogue: The lunch rush ended with the resort officially recognizing Nene's 'Husband Staffing Model' as an event-only volunteer program. Nene considers the words 'event-only' negotiable.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: NePoLaBo solved the staffing shortage. The HR department has requested that Nene stop solving things.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Use Myth to reroute guests around maintenance after Ina draws a shortcut that develops opinions about geometry.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Construction has closed the shortest path to the beach. Amelia has a clipboard and magnifying glass, Gura is timing the detour, Calli is moving barriers, and Ina has drawn a tiny door on the map labeled 'shorter way.'

steps.prompt: The guest detour adds twelve minutes. Ina jokes that management can just approve her drawn shortcut.

options.resultDialogue: You stamp the doodle. A door appears in the blank wall beside the map. Gura stares at it. 'A.' Amelia checks both sides of the wall. 'That is not structurally possible.' Calli shrugs. 'Still shorter.' Ina quietly adds a doorknob to her drawing. The real door grows one.

options.text: Ask Amelia to verify it first
options.resultDialogue: Amelia measures the wall, checks the blueprint, and declares, 'There is absolutely no door here.' The wall opens behind her. Gura points. 'Detective.' Amelia turns around very slowly. 'I would like to revise my statement.'

Calli moves the barriers and tells everyone to walk around. The new path behaves normally for eight seconds, then a painted arrow on Ina's map rotates toward a service hallway. Calli looks at you. 'Your island is backseat managing me.'

steps.prompt: The strange shortcut works, but each trip exits somewhere slightly different.

options.text: Turn it into a guided attraction
options.resultDialogue: Amelia assigns each guest a numbered group. Door 1 exits at the beach. Door 2 exits beside the café. Door 3 exits behind Calli, who was standing in front of Door 3. Calli turns around. 'Okay, that's rude.' Gura asks for Door 4. Amelia says, 'There will not be a Door 4.' Ina starts drawing.

Ina erases the door from the map. The real doorway begins shrinking. Gura dives through at the last second and returns holding the same clipboard you are carrying. She looks at yours, then hers. 'Manager, I think I stole tomorrow.' Amelia takes both clipboards away.

steps.prompt: Guests are safely routed. The map asks whether the shortcut should be retained as a temporary management feature.

options.resultDialogue: You reject it. The wall becomes solid again. Amelia immediately tapes a paper labeled DOOR WAS HERE to the spot. Calli asks why. 'Evidence.' Gura writes WAS IT? underneath.
options.completionDialogue: Myth restored a normal guest route and closed the impossible shortcut. Amelia has opened a case against one wall.

options.resultDialogue: You approve supervised use. The map prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED and adds a tiny icon shaped like your clipboard. Ina smiles. 'It likes your approval stamp.' Amelia says, 'Please do not phrase it like that.' Gura stamps the map twice. Nothing happens. 'Rude.'
options.completionDialogue: Myth kept the strange shortcut as a supervised detour. It behaves perfectly whenever the Manager is watching, which Amelia considers more suspicious than if it did not.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Myth kept beach traffic moving. The resort may now contain one wall with a personal relationship to paperwork.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Protect Anya's nap while Ollie discovers what happens when management makes 'quiet hours' an absolute rule.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Anya is asleep behind the hotel reception desk after volunteering for exactly seven minutes. Ollie has decided this means she is now the entire front-desk staff and is greeting guests at a volume normally used for emergency sirens.

steps.prompt: The lunch check-in rush begins while Anya sleeps. What temporary lobby rule do you set?

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'Nobody wakes Anya.' Every speaker switches off. Elevator bells become tiny flashes of light. Ollie opens her mouth to shout—and no sound comes out. Her eyes widen. She points at you, then at her throat, then begins screaming silently with increasing professionalism.

You tell Ollie she may speak only at library volume. A glowing volume meter appears above her head. 'HEL—' RED. She whispers, 'hello.' GREEN. Ollie looks personally betrayed by acoustics. Anya turns over in her chair and gives a sleepy thumbs-up.

You order the reception desk moved away from Anya. The entire desk slides across the marble floor by itself, carrying Ollie, three suitcases, and one confused tourist. Anya remains asleep in the chair it left behind. Ollie rides the desk like a ship. Silently, because she remembers the first option exists conceptually.

steps.prompt: Quiet-hour enforcement spreads through the hotel. Even the ice machine is dispensing cubes apologetically.

options.text: Market it as a silent spa hour
options.resultDialogue: You turn the problem into a luxury experience. Guests whisper, the lights dim, and Ollie communicates using enormous cue cards. Her first card reads I AM SUFFERING. The second reads FIVE STARS. Anya rolls over and keeps sleeping.

options.text: Wake Anya and cancel the rule
options.resultDialogue: Ollie tiptoes over and pokes Anya. Anya opens one eye. 'Why is everyone miming?' The instant she sits up, every suppressed sound plays at once: elevator dings, lobby music, Ollie's missing screams, and a blender from the kitchen. Ollie is knocked backward by her own backlog.

steps.prompt: The hotel is functional again. What happens to the quiet-hour policy?

options.resultDialogue: You approve one supervised quiet hour. Ollie receives a printed schedule and points at it in horror. Anya pockets a copy. 'Useful.' Ollie points at her betrayal. Anya has already gone back to sleep.
options.completionDialogue: holoro established a daily quiet hour that guests immediately loved and Ollie immediately began campaigning against.

options.resultDialogue: You cancel the policy. Ollie inhales for what is clearly going to be a victory scream. Anya raises one finger without opening her eyes. Ollie slowly exhales instead. The hotel has developed a stronger authority than management.
options.completionDialogue: holoro restored normal hotel operations. Anya slept through nearly the entire incident and later rated management's crisis response 'quiet.'

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoro kept the hotel running around one nap. Ollie now understands that silence can be a hostile environment.

evening.title: Day 9 — Approved by Management
evening.openingDialogue: Evening operations become increasingly literal: stages move when asked, weather accepts requests, and a vending machine acquires a health bar. No findings occur today; the only mystery is why resort systems keep recording the Manager's choices.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Move an evening performance closer to Luna's VIP deck without interpreting her request too literally.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Luna is seated on the VIP deck with a tiny fan. Kanata is moving speakers, Towa is checking cables, Watame is rehearsing, and the stage is a perfectly reasonable thirty meters away.

steps.prompt: Luna squints at the stage. 'Too far, nanora. Manager, bring it closer.' How do you interpret that?

options.resultDialogue: You point to the chairs. Before staff can touch them, every chair slides toward the stage in perfect rows. Luna remains behind on her throne. She stares at the empty deck. 'Manager.' Towa looks at you. 'You moved the wrong side of the equation.'

You say, 'Bring the stage closer.' The entire stage begins rolling across the plaza. Kanata grabs the front edge with both hands. 'WHY DOES IT HAVE WHEELS NOW?!' Watame keeps singing while slowly passing the snack stalls. Towa sprints after the power cable.

You hand Luna binoculars. She looks through them. 'Closer.' The stage does not move. Luna lowers the binoculars. 'Acceptable technology.' Kanata wipes sweat from her forehead. Towa whispers, 'We survived grammar.'

steps.prompt: The audience loves the moving-stage concept and starts cheering for it to come closer too.

options.resultDialogue: Kanata plants her feet and stops the stage with both hands. The wheels keep spinning, carving two neat lines into the pavement. Watame waves from center stage. 'Kanata-chan, you're part of the set now!' Kanata, still holding several tons of platform: 'PLEASE END THE SONG.'

options.text: Turn it into Luna's royal float
options.resultDialogue: You let the stage roll slowly around the plaza. Luna transfers her throne aboard and begins waving. Towa walks beside the emergency brake. Watame performs like nothing is strange. A guest asks whether this was planned. Towa says, 'From this second onward, yes.'

steps.prompt: The concert ends. The stage control panel displays MANAGEMENT POSITIONING REQUEST COMPLETE.

options.resultDialogue: Towa locks every wheel, then adds chains, blocks, and a handwritten sign reading DO NOT LISTEN TO LUNA. Luna reads it. 'Towa.' Towa flips the sign over. The other side says PLEASE.
options.completionDialogue: holoForce finished the concert with the stage safely anchored. Luna has submitted a request for a moving castle next.

options.resultDialogue: You approve controlled movement for future events. Kanata asks, 'Who controls it?' The panel lights up when you touch it. Everyone looks at your hand. You slowly remove it. Watame says, 'Manager has stage powers now.' Towa: 'Do not encourage the island.'
options.completionDialogue: holoForce preserved the mobile-stage feature for controlled parades. Towa has added 'Do not phrase requests casually around Manager' to the safety manual.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoForce completed the performance. The stage is no longer approaching anyone without written consent.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Give Kobo one tiny weather adjustment. Kaela has already prepared for the worst.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: The pool deck is too hot for the evening splash show. Kaela is checking shade structures, Zeta is monitoring the crowd, and Kobo is pointing angrily at a perfectly clear sky.

steps.prompt: Kobo demands 'rain, but only on the pool.' What do you approve?

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'Fine. Rain on the pool only.' A single cloud appears directly above the water and begins raining inside the pool boundary. Kobo points at it with both hands. 'SEE?! PROFESSIONAL WEATHER!' Zeta looks up. 'There was no cloud thirty seconds ago.' Kaela puts on a raincoat. 'Now there is.'

Kaela turns on the misting system. Kobo crosses her arms. 'Fake rain.' Zeta adjusts one nozzle. It immediately follows Kobo when she walks. Kobo stops. The nozzle stops. Zeta: 'The sprinkler has chosen a client.'

Zeta announces a '60% chance of highly localized rain.' Kobo asks, 'Where is the 40%?' Zeta points at the dry chairs. A tiny cloud forms over the pool anyway. Zeta lowers the forecast card. 'I dislike being retroactively correct.'

steps.prompt: Kobo realizes the cloud reacts to requests and immediately asks for thunder applause.

options.resultDialogue: A tiny rumble sounds after Kobo's cannonball. The crowd cheers. Kobo jumps again. Thunder. Again. Thunder. Kaela counts seven jumps, walks over, and physically removes Kobo from the diving board. The cloud gives one disappointed rumble.

You forbid more requests. Kobo points at the cloud. 'Go home!' The cloud immediately drifts away. Zeta watches it leave. 'Manager, I believe we have proven the ban was also a request.' Kaela: 'Do not say that near her.'

steps.prompt: The splash show succeeds. Kaela asks whether to preserve localized weather control.

options.resultDialogue: You cancel the weather setting. The sky clears. Kobo shakes one fist upward. 'COWARD SKY!' A single raindrop lands on her forehead. Zeta writes, 'Possible retaliation.' Kaela crosses it out. 'No.'
options.completionDialogue: holoh3ro completed the splash show under ordinary weather. Kobo is now in a personal dispute with one cloud.

options.resultDialogue: You authorize controlled pool weather. The panel prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED. Kaela reads it, then looks at you. 'Use exact words next time.' Kobo raises her hand. 'Manager, can we have snow?' Kaela lowers her hand for her.
options.completionDialogue: holoh3ro kept localized pool weather as a supervised attraction feature. Kobo has been banned from requesting seasons.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoh3ro finished the evening splash show. Weather is once again being treated as an equipment category.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Fix one broken vending machine after Aqua describes customer service as a boss fight.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: A vending machine near the night pool has swallowed twelve guest coins. Aqua is crouched in front of it like a raid leader, Shion is threatening it with magic, and Choco has opened a first-aid kit despite nobody being injured yet.

steps.prompt: The machine refuses refunds. Aqua says, 'Fine. Treat it like a boss fight.' What do you authorize?

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'Okay. Boss fight.' A red health bar appears above the vending machine. Battle music starts. Aqua goes completely still. Shion slowly grins. Choco opens a second first-aid kit. 'I knew preparation would be rewarded.'

Shion taps the machine and says, 'May every drink you hold become warm.' The temperature display flashes 99°C, panics, and immediately refunds all twelve coins. Aqua stares. 'You threatened it.' Shion smiles. 'Customer service.'

Choco presses the service button and speaks politely. The machine dispenses one apology coupon. Aqua points. 'It has dialogue options.' Shion presses the button again. The machine prints PLEASE STOP. Choco: 'We have established boundaries.'

steps.prompt: The machine now behaves exactly like the solution you approved, and the guests have formed a spectator circle.

options.resultDialogue: Aqua calls phases, Shion fires harmless spark attacks, and Choco announces 'mechanical damage only.' At 1% HP, the vending machine begins flashing ENRAGE. Aqua screams, presses REFUND, and the health bar drops to zero. Every drink dispenses at once. Aqua raises both fists. 'WORLD FIRST!'

You unplug the machine. The boss music stops. The health bar remains floating in midair for three seconds, then displays DISCONNECTED — TECHNICAL VICTORY. Aqua points at it. 'I'll take it.' Shion boos. Choco starts distributing the refunded drinks.

steps.prompt: The repaired screen briefly shows: MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT INDEXED. Then it returns to the drink menu.

options.resultDialogue: Aqua is too busy signing a napkin labeled RAID CLEAR. Shion asks if the next broken appliance can be PvP. Choco says, 'No.' The refrigerator behind her produces a tiny health bar. Choco turns around. It disappears.
options.completionDialogue: Gen 2 restored the vending machine and entertained half the pool deck in the process. Management has declined to recognize appliance combat as an official sport.

options.resultDialogue: You copy MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT INDEXED into the incident report. Shion reads it over your shoulder. 'That sounds ominous.' Aqua points at the free drinks. 'It also sounds profitable.' Choco closes the report. 'Those are not mutually exclusive.'
options.completionDialogue: Gen 2 restored the vending machine and preserved the clearest clue yet that the resort is somehow cataloging Manager-approved decisions.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Gen 2 defeated customer service. The vending machine has returned to normal and no longer has visible hit points.

days.storyBeat: The resort stops merely obeying individual decisions and begins 'helping' with them. Rematches schedule themselves, applause edits architecture, words rewrite attractions, queues become nations, and safety promises behave like contracts. Guest satisfaction remains annoyingly high.

morning.title: Day 10 — The Island Is Helping
morning.openingDialogue: The Manager arrives to three messages thanking them for 'successful precedent deployment.' Before anyone can ask what that means, the arcade schedules infinity, Miko invents a road, and FLOW GLOW discovers applause can raise a stage.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Stop one friendly arcade rematch from becoming a permanent resort calendar event.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: The repaired arcade has reopened. Fubuki is holding yesterday's rulebook, Mio has brought a calm smile that already looks endangered, Okayu has snacks, and Korone is pointing at a racing cabinet. 'Again.'

steps.prompt: Korone asks for one rematch. The arcade calendar immediately schedules it.

options.resultDialogue: You approve exactly one. The screen prints REMATCH 1 OF 1. Korone wins, turns around, and says, 'Again.' The screen updates to REMATCH 2 OF 1. Mio stares at the fraction. Fubuki whispers, 'We have escaped arithmetic.'

Fubuki adds 'Best of three, unless friendship requires more data.' The cabinet prints a twenty-seven-match bracket. Mio takes the pen from her. 'Friendship does not require this much data.' Okayu looks at the snack table. 'I can survive twenty-seven.'

You say, 'No more rematches.' The event board instantly creates a new team named NO MORE REMATCHES and schedules them against GAMERS at 10:30. Korone points at the board. 'We have opponent.' Mio closes her eyes. Fubuki starts laughing so hard she has to sit down.

steps.prompt: Every use of the word 'again' is now creating another match.

options.resultDialogue: Mio posts a temporary ban. Korone tries 'one more.' New match. 'Encore.' New match. 'Repeat.' New match. Fubuki begins taking notes. Mio tears the notes in half. Okayu: 'We may need to ban language.'

Okayu walks to the power switch. Korone grabs her arm. 'One more?' Okayu holds up a rice ball. Korone looks at the cabinet, then the rice ball, then the cabinet. '...food first.' The calendar stops generating matches. Mio whispers, 'We found the kill switch.'

steps.prompt: The arcade asks whether REMATCH MODE should remain available for guest events.

options.resultDialogue: You turn it off. Korone immediately challenges Fubuki manually. Mio points at the sign. 'That defeats the purpose.' Fubuki smiles. 'The machine is fixed. The people are not.'
options.completionDialogue: Gamers restored the arcade calendar. Rematches must once again be scheduled by humans, which has not reduced the number of rematches.

options.resultDialogue: You keep one button labeled AGAIN. Korone presses it. Mio covers the button. Korone presses Mio's hand. The machine registers the input. Fubuki falls against the wall laughing. Okayu offers Mio a snack as compensation.
options.completionDialogue: Gamers kept a supervised rematch feature. The word 'supervised' currently means Mio is standing directly in front of Korone.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Gamers completed the arcade reopening. The bracket has been reduced from infinite to merely unreasonable.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Miko improve pedestrian flow after the island begins treating 'elite route' as a civil-engineering specification.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Miko is standing beside a slow moving walkway with a marker. Suisei has a tool belt that includes an axe for reasons nobody has challenged. AZKi is mapping guest traffic on a tablet.

steps.prompt: The walkway is congested. Miko proposes an 'Elite Expressway.' How much authority do you give her?

options.resultDialogue: Miko draws one pink arrow. The floor extends into a second moving lane beside the first. AZKi's map updates by itself. Miko throws both arms up. 'ELITE URBAN PLANNING!' Suisei checks where the lane ends. 'Kitchen window.' Miko lowers one arm. 'Mixed-use development.'

options.text: Let AZKi map a proper route
options.resultDialogue: AZKi plots a clean detour around the crowd. The navigation signs update instantly—then add MIKO SCENIC OPTION underneath. Miko points proudly. 'The system respects choice.' Suisei: 'The scenic option goes through a storage closet.'

options.text: Ask Suisei to remove bad signs
options.resultDialogue: Suisei quietly removes three confusing arrows. A fourth sign grows out of the floor behind her. She removes it. Two more appear. Miko whispers, 'The route is fighting back.' Suisei smiles. 'Good.' AZKi increases the safe distance around both of them.

steps.prompt: The new route begins adapting itself to guest traffic—and to Miko's commentary.

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'Miko, don't say anything about the route.' She nods solemnly. A guest asks where it goes. Miko shakes with effort. Suisei leans closer. 'You can do it.' Miko lasts four seconds. 'IT GOES TO THE ELITE—' A new ramp unfolds. AZKi: 'Four seconds was better than expected.'

Suisei points at the beach. 'Straight there.' Every unnecessary turn retracts at once. Miko stares at the clean line. 'Where is the personality?' Suisei points at the axe. 'Removed.' AZKi marks the route 'efficient, slightly threatening.'

steps.prompt: The route is usable. Should the Elite Expressway stay?

options.resultDialogue: You keep Suisei's direct version. Miko installs a sign reading ELITE EXPRESSWAY anyway. AZKi adds smaller text: 'Normal walkway.' Miko covers it. AZKi replaces it. This becomes the attraction's first maintenance cycle.
options.completionDialogue: Gen 0 opened a safe fast lane. It is officially a normal walkway and unofficially Miko's greatest infrastructure achievement.

options.resultDialogue: You approve the scenic route. The terminal flashes MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED.

You order the walkway returned to factory layout. The extra lanes fold away. Miko watches her infrastructure disappear. 'They hated innovation.' Suisei: 'The kitchen staff hated pedestrians.' Miko: 'Same thing.'
options.completionDialogue: Gen 0 returned the walkway to normal and ended Miko's brief career in autonomous civil engineering.

steps.prompt: The system recognizes Miko's earlier shortcut history and labels the scenic lane HERITAGE ROUTE.

options.resultDialogue: Miko becomes completely unbearable. 'HISTORY HAS VALIDATED ME!' Suisei reads the plaque. 'It says 'preserved due to repeated management approval.'' Miko points at you. 'History has validated us!' AZKi quietly photographs your regret.
options.completionDialogue: Gen 0 preserved the Elite Expressway as a supervised heritage route. The island appears to remember that management previously tolerated Miko's shortcuts.

options.resultDialogue: You press OVERRIDE. The plaque retracts. Miko falls to her knees. 'CENSORSHIP!' Suisei picks her up by the back of her shirt and carries her away from the control panel.
options.completionDialogue: Gen 0 removed the heritage designation from Miko's shortcut. Miko is preparing an appeal to future historians.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Gen 0 fixed pedestrian traffic. Miko has not fixed her understanding of zoning.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Stop FLOW GLOW's crowd-response system from turning enthusiasm into structural engineering.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: The morning stage has been upgraded with live audience-response sensors. Su is watching the meters, Chihaya has the program, Vivi has the microphone, Niko has discovered the CHEER MULTIPLIER, and Riona is pretending she does not care how high her entrance score is.

steps.prompt: The crowd cheers for Riona's entrance. The stage physically rises twenty centimeters.

options.resultDialogue: Su lowers the sensitivity. Niko whispers 'Riona!' into the crowd. The stage rises another ten centimeters. Su turns toward her. Niko points at a random tourist. 'Saboteur.' Chihaya: 'You are holding the multiplier.'

Vivi shouts, 'MAKE SOME NOISE!' The audience roars. The stage rises past the lighting rig. Riona grips the railing while maintaining her pose. 'I refuse to look concerned.' Niko looks down. 'You look expensive.'

Chihaya gives the crowd score cards instead. The stage stops rising. Then a tourist holds up 10/10 and one spotlight becomes ten spotlights. Su looks at the panel. 'It has generalized the concept of approval.' Niko holds up eleven.

steps.prompt: Every positive audience reaction now improves something physically: louder bass, taller stage, more lights.

options.resultDialogue: Riona takes the mic. 'Tell us what you dislike.' The crowd goes silent. Niko shouts, 'The stage is too tall!' It drops half a meter. Vivi: 'The bass is too weak!' The bass doubles. Su grabs her. 'THAT WAS A COMPLIMENT SHAPED WRONG.'

options.text: Turn it into a controlled finale
options.resultDialogue: Chihaya schedules exactly one ten-second cheer. The crowd roars, the stage rises, smoke blooms, lights sweep the plaza—and Su slams the limiter at the peak. The whole structure settles perfectly. Riona exhales. 'I was never worried.' Niko shows her a photo of the railing dents.

steps.prompt: The sensors ask whether audience approval should remain an operational input.

options.resultDialogue: You disable physical response. Niko boos. Nothing moves. She boos louder. Still nothing. Su smiles. 'Technology has stopped caring about you.' Niko presses a hand to her chest. 'Cruel.'
options.completionDialogue: FLOW GLOW restored the stage to ordinary physics. Audience applause now affects only performers, as nature intended.

options.resultDialogue: You allow lights and harmless streamers but lock out structural movement. Vivi tests a cheer; glitter rains down. Riona smiles. Niko cheers again. A second glitter burst targets only Niko. Su: 'I did not program revenge.'
options.completionDialogue: FLOW GLOW kept audience-responsive effects while removing the part where applause could renovate the venue.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: FLOW GLOW completed the stage test. The audience may continue influencing morale, but not load-bearing architecture.

noon.title: Day 10 — Administrative Reality
noon.openingDialogue: At noon, paperwork becomes dangerous. Justice classifications affect security, Advent adjectives affect attractions, and Risu discovers that the resort is perfectly willing to automate capitalism.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Help Justice test a filing system that has begun treating Gigi's labels as legally meaningful.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Justice has received a new incident-classification terminal. Elizabeth has organized forms by severity, Cecilia is testing the database, Raora is drawing category icons, and Gigi has already labeled one empty folder SUSPICIOUS.

steps.prompt: Cecilia asks for three legitimate incident categories. Gigi volunteers first.

options.resultDialogue: You approve SUSPICIOUS. Every unlabeled object in the office receives a yellow S sticker. Elizabeth looks at her tea. SUSPICIOUS. Her chair. SUSPICIOUS. Gigi points at the terminal. 'IT UNDERSTANDS PROFILING.' Cecilia: 'It understands one word. Unfortunately.'

Cecilia creates Mechanical, Guest, Weather, and Manager-Induced. Elizabeth stops writing. 'Why is Manager-Induced a standard category?' Cecilia displays the week's incident count. You try to close the graph. It expands.

Elizabeth reads the old case file. 'Management previously recognized organized avian activity.' Gigi slams a BIRD stamp onto the terminal. Outside, three seagulls immediately receive red outline markers on the security camera. Raora whispers, 'Oh no. We made crime UI.'

steps.prompt: The classification terminal begins changing how security staff react to whatever category is selected.

options.resultDialogue: Elizabeth writes careful definitions. Gigi adds 'looks guilty' to SUSPICIOUS. Elizabeth crosses it out. Gigi adds 'acts bird' to BIRD. Elizabeth crosses it out. Raora draws a tiny legal wig on the icon. Elizabeth pauses. 'That may stay.'

Gigi labels herself SUSPICIOUS. The office door locks her inside. She beams. 'IT WORKS!' Elizabeth unlocks it. Gigi labels Elizabeth MANAGEMENT-INDUCED. The lights turn red. Cecilia picks up the label maker and removes its batteries.

steps.prompt: The system asks which category definitions should become permanent.

options.resultDialogue: You retain Mechanical, Guest, Weather, and Safety. Gigi's SUSPICIOUS folder is rejected. She immediately creates a physical cardboard box labeled SUSPICIOUS instead. Cecilia: 'Analog systems remain our greatest vulnerability.'
options.completionDialogue: Justice stabilized the classification system. Gigi has been denied digital taxonomy privileges and has moved to cardboard.

options.resultDialogue: You preserve one joke category for staff morale. The terminal prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED. Elizabeth sighs. 'I refuse to ask why the island respects comedic jurisprudence.' Gigi raises a gavel she did not have a moment ago. 'COURT IS BACK.'
options.completionDialogue: Justice kept one absurd classification as an event-only category. The resort has now demonstrated that jokes can survive contact with administrative law.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Justice finished the classification test. The database is cleaner. Gigi is not.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Write attraction copy with Advent after the resort starts taking adjectives as design requirements.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Shiori is editing the resort brochure. Nerissa is reading descriptions aloud, Bijou is adding 'FINAL BOSS' to places she likes, and Fuwawa and Mococo are stamping everything PAW-APPROVED.

steps.prompt: The mini-golf description needs one sentence. Who writes it?

options.resultDialogue: Shiori writes: 'A winding course where every corner hides a new challenge.' The mini-golf walls immediately grow three extra corners. Shiori stares at the paper. 'That is an unusually literal editor.' Bijou adds, 'And final boss.' A stone face appears on Hole 18.

Nerissa writes 'hauntingly beautiful.' A soft choir begins singing from the windmill obstacle. Fuwawa looks inside. Nobody is there. Mococo: 'BAU...?' Nerissa slowly crosses out 'hauntingly.' The choir becomes merely beautiful.

The twins stamp PUPPY-APPROVED. Every directional arrow on the course becomes a paw print. Bijou follows them directly into the sand trap. 'The puppies betrayed me!' Fuwawa: 'The paws were metaphorical!' Mococo: 'They are VERY physical now!'

steps.prompt: The brochure is clearly rewriting attraction details as fast as Advent edits them.

options.resultDialogue: Shiori replaces everything with 'Mini-golf course. Contains eighteen holes.' The extra corners retract, the choir stops, and Hole 18 loses its face. Bijou stares at the page. 'You killed the lore.' Shiori nods. 'With documentation.'
You approve 'sparkling.' The course gains harmless glittering lights. Nerissa smiles. Bijou writes 'terrifyingly sparkling.' Shiori catches her pen one centimeter above the paper. 'No adverb crimes.'

steps.prompt: The brochure editor asks whether descriptive changes should remain enabled.

options.resultDialogue: You turn it off. Bijou writes FINAL BOSS three more times. Nothing happens. She looks devastated. FUWAMOCO pat her shoulders from both sides. Shiori locks the brochure in a drawer labeled WORDS ARE POWER, APPARENTLY.
options.completionDialogue: Advent restored the brochure to ordinary marketing. Adjectives no longer possess construction permits.

options.resultDialogue: You allow cosmetic terms only. Nerissa tests 'warm.' The lights soften. 'Colorful.' Banners brighten. Bijou whispers 'explosive.' Nothing happens. She clicks her tongue. Shiori: 'The filter works.'
options.completionDialogue: Advent kept a filtered brochure system that can alter harmless presentation details. Bijou has begun compiling a dictionary of words the filter hates.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Advent completed the brochure. The resort is now legally protected from adjectives above a certain threat level.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Stop Risu from proving that even moonlight can be monetized when the island handles billing automatically.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: The shaded lounge is reopening for afternoon recovery. Moona is adjusting soft lighting, Iofi is painting signs, and Risu has placed a tiny card reader beside a chair labeled PREMIUM MOONLIGHT.

steps.prompt: Risu claims premium seating deserves premium moonlight. What do you do?

options.resultDialogue: You say, 'Sure, charge for moonlight.' A turnstile rises around the brightest patch of light. Risu freezes, then slowly smiles. Moona: 'No.' Risu: 'The island has spoken.' Iofi reads the new price screen. 'The island has also added tax.' Risu's smile vanishes.

You write FREE LIGHT. The card reader disappears into the floor. Risu drops to her knees. 'My business model!' Moona increases the brightness around her. 'Here. Free emotional support.' Iofi adds a small sign: BASIC SUNLIGHT INCLUDED.

options.text: Let Iofi create premium art instead
options.resultDialogue: Iofi paints glowing moon patterns around the lounge. The system asks STANDARD OR PREMIUM ART. Risu answers PREMIUM before anyone else. The paintings grow velvet ropes. Iofi stares. 'I did not paint capitalism.'

steps.prompt: Guests are actually paying for ridiculous light tiers, and the resort billing system is taking a cut.

options.resultDialogue: You order refunds. Risu hands them out while staring at the system's 30% infrastructure levy. 'It taxed my moon.' Moona: 'It was never your moon.' Risu points at the receipt. 'Then why did it take my money?!'

options.text: Turn it into optional charity seating
options.resultDialogue: You redirect the fee to resort maintenance. Guests keep paying because the premium seats have better photos. Risu reads the donation total. 'I invented philanthropy by accident.' Iofi: 'You invented a chair.'

steps.prompt: The lounge is stable. What pricing rule survives?

options.resultDialogue: You ban light fees specifically. Risu asks, 'What about premium darkness?' Moona turns off her lamp. Risu becomes a silhouette. Iofi writes NO beside her before she can finish the pitch.
options.completionDialogue: AREA 15 reopened the lounge with free light and ordinary seating. Risu is exploring business opportunities unrelated to photons.

options.resultDialogue: You allow paid decorated photo zones but not the light itself. Risu nods. 'We sell location, not moon.' Iofi approves. Moona asks, 'Did we just regulate lunar commerce?' Nobody answers.
options.completionDialogue: AREA 15 kept optional paid photo zones while declaring moonlight a public resource. The policy exists because this conversation happened.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: AREA 15 completed the lounge reopening. Moonlight remains free, to the disappointment of one squirrel.

evening.title: Day 10 — Terms and Conditions Apply
evening.openingDialogue: By evening, the resort is enforcing queue borders, printing insurance policies, and honoring Subaru's verbal safety guarantee like a binding contract. No findings occur; management is too busy trying to stop ordinary sentences from becoming features.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Let ReGLOSS fix one messy dinner queue without accidentally founding a country.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: The dinner market has three intersecting lines and zero agreement about where they begin. Hajime is already drawing lanes, Ririka has pricing ideas, Kanade has a microphone, Raden has found the situation anthropologically fascinating, and Ao is trying to look uninvolved.

steps.prompt: Hajime says, 'Every line needs a border.' The floor immediately paints one.

options.resultDialogue: Hajime points left. The floor arrows slide left. She points right. They slide right. Kanade steps across one line and a tiny buzzer sounds. 'Border violation!' she shouts. Hajime: 'Do not make it fun.' Ririka is already printing priority visas.

Ririka says, 'Not priority access. Diplomatic passage.' A booth rises from the floor reading QUEUE VISA OFFICE. Raden adjusts her glasses. 'We have invented bureaucracy before dinner.' Ao: 'Can I be foreign?' Hajime: 'No.'

Kanade grabs the mic. 'WELCOME TO THE SOVEREIGN NATION OF DINNER!' The signs immediately change to QUEUE NATION — POPULATION 143. Raden turns to you. 'Manager. Words have consequences.' Kanade: 'I HAVE CITIZENS!'

steps.prompt: Guests are treating the queue lanes like border crossings and asking for stamps.

options.resultDialogue: You let guests collect three harmless stamps while waiting. Ririka creates express visas, Hajime sets traffic flow, and Raden writes a two-paragraph history of the nation that began eleven minutes ago. Ao poses for the passport photo booth. 'Finally. Statesmanship.'
You announce, 'Queue Nation is dissolved.' The PA replies NATIONAL STATUS UPDATED: FORMER QUEUE NATION. Kanade gasps. 'We have history!' Raden closes her notebook. 'Unfortunately, yes.'

steps.prompt: Dinner service is finally moving. What stays after tonight?

options.resultDialogue: You preserve the efficient arrows and remove every border booth. Ririka tries to keep one tiny embassy. Hajime removes it with one hand. Kanade sings a solemn national anthem for a country that lasted twenty-three minutes.
options.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS restored dinner service with a clean queue system. Queue Nation has ceased to exist except in Raden's extremely detailed historical record.

options.text: Keep the stamp game for events
options.resultDialogue: You approve the stamp game. The terminal prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED: TEMPORARY MICROSTATE ACTIVITY. Everyone stares. Ririka smiles first. 'Merchandise.' Hajime says, 'No currency.' Ririka's smile becomes smaller but survives.
options.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS kept Queue Nation as a supervised event game. Management has explicitly prohibited borders, currency, embassies, and whatever Kanade was about to suggest.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: ReGLOSS solved the dinner queue by briefly inventing geopolitics.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Handle an attraction safety review after Pekora discovers the resort will print insurance policies for things management approves.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Pekora has proposed a new explosive target game. Flare has already confiscated two fuses. Noel is carrying the reinforced target frame, and Marine is posing beside a blank sponsorship board waiting for someone to make a mistake.

steps.prompt: Pekora says the attraction is safe because 'we'll insure it.' How do you respond?

options.resultDialogue: Pekora freezes. Then she puts on fake glasses and a moustache. 'Good evening-peko. I am Ms. Usada from Usada Mutual.' Flare stares. 'Take those off.' A printer behind Pekora activates and produces an actual policy. Marine gasps. 'Senchou wants a corporate title.'

You demand actual coverage before launch. The resort terminal prints OWNER: USADA PEKORA. INSURER: PENDING. Pekora points at Noel. 'Strong company-peko?' Noel smiles. Flare says, 'Do not drag Noel into financial crime.' Marine raises her hand. 'Senchou has maritime experience.' Flare: 'Also no.'

You say no explosives. Pekora nods. 'Understood-peko.' Flare points at three very visible fuses Pekora has already wired into the target frame and removes them one by one. Pekora looks offended. 'Those were decorative.' Noel examines one. 'This one says MAIN.'

steps.prompt: The resort has accepted the insurance concept and begins auto-filing claims during the safety test.

options.resultDialogue: Noel taps the reinforced target to check stability. The frame survives; the wall behind it moves six centimeters. A printer instantly produces CLAIM #1: STRUCTURAL DISPLACEMENT. Pekora grabs it. 'Act of knight-peko.' Noel: 'Sorry!' Flare: 'No apologizing to the insurer.'

Marine steps in front of the sign. 'Senchou guarantees a thrilling yet responsible experience!' The terminal prints GUARANTOR: HOUSHOU MARINE. Marine's smile dies. Pekora slides the policy toward her. 'Sign here-peko.' Marine: 'Senchou retracts the adjective responsible.'

steps.prompt: The attraction can open only if management decides what happens to the insurance system.

options.resultDialogue: You cancel the policy. Pekora tears off the moustache. 'Corporate death-peko.' Flare opens a drawer and removes five spare moustaches. Pekora gasps. 'Trade secrets!' Marine takes one for a commemorative photo.
options.completionDialogue: Fantasy opened a safe non-explosive target game and dissolved Usada Mutual before it could become legally interesting.

options.text: Keep insurance as a joke booth
options.resultDialogue: You keep Usada Mutual as a clearly fictional photo booth. The terminal stamps MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED: ENTERTAINMENT ONLY. Pekora reads only the first three words and cheers. Flare circles ENTERTAINMENT ONLY in red. Marine signs the backdrop 'Senchou, Chief Risk Pirate.'
options.completionDialogue: Fantasy preserved Usada Mutual as a harmless comedy booth. Pekora continues introducing herself as CEO whenever Flare is out of earshot.

options.resultDialogue: The terminal imports the PekoMari refund desk and immediately lists outstanding liabilities. Pekora watches the number climb. 'Turn it off-peko.' Flare folds her arms. Marine reads the total and slowly removes her corporate hat. 'Senchou has retired from finance.'
options.completionDialogue: Fantasy connected Usada Mutual to the previous claims desk and bankrupted the fictional company in under ninety seconds.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Fantasy completed the safety review. The attraction is safe. Pekora's corporate future is not.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Run a night boat tour with Ayame and Subaru after Subaru makes the catastrophic promise that nothing will go wrong.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Subaru is briefing guests for a calm harbor tour. Ayame is already seated with a drink, looking completely relaxed. The boat is inspected, the weather is clear, and absolutely nobody should say anything that tempts fate.

steps.prompt: Subaru raises the microphone. 'Tonight, nothing can possibly go wrong!' The boat console lights up: SAFETY GUARANTEE ACCEPTED.

options.text: Tell Subaru to take it back
options.resultDialogue: Subaru grabs the mic. 'I TAKE IT BACK!' The console replies GUARANTEE CANNOT BE REDUCED DURING ACTIVE SERVICE. Ayame giggles. 'You signed a contract with destiny.' Subaru points at you. 'MANAGER, CANCEL DESTINY.'

You let the tour depart. A wave approaches the boat, stops at an invisible line, and turns ninety degrees into an empty splash zone. Subaru stares. Ayame raises her cup. 'Very safe.' Subaru whispers, 'Too safe.'

Ayame casually tosses a foam ball overboard. A rescue ring launches itself, catches the ball, and returns it to her lap. She tosses it again. Same result. Subaru grabs the ball. 'STOP STRESS-TESTING REALITY!' Ayame: 'But it is cute.'

steps.prompt: The safety guarantee begins overcorrecting every tiny risk.

options.resultDialogue: You set the console to NORMAL. It refuses because Subaru promised 'nothing.' A napkin begins sliding off a table; a tiny air jet pushes it back. Ayame watches the napkin. 'Strong opponent.' Subaru: 'DO NOT CHALLENGE THE SAFETY SYSTEM.'

You announce an early return. The boat teleports three meters sideways into its berth rather than risk docking manually. Subaru grips the railing. 'THAT WAS LESS SAFE EMOTIONALLY!' Ayame steps off. 'Efficient.'

steps.prompt: The final screen asks whether to save Subaru's 'zero-risk' guarantee.

options.resultDialogue: You erase it. A normal wave gently rocks the boat. Subaru exhales in relief, then realizes she is relieved by danger. 'This island has changed me.' Ayame pats her shoulder. 'Character development.'
options.completionDialogue: Gen 2 completed the harbor tour and removed the impossible zero-risk guarantee. Normal manageable danger has returned.

options.resultDialogue: You preserve the guarantee for emergencies only. The system prints MANAGEMENT PRECEDENT ACCEPTED. Subaru stares at the words. 'Why does it keep saying that?' Ayame smiles. 'Because Manager keeps setting precedents.' Subaru slowly turns toward you.
options.completionDialogue: Gen 2 preserved the zero-risk system for emergency evacuations. Subaru has been instructed never to promise anything on a microphone again.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Gen 2 completed the night tour. Subaru's confidence is now classified as a controllable hazard.

days.storyBeat: The impossible fourth pier becomes physically accessible. Morning is spent giving it names, borders, and unwanted ownership claims; Noon reaches the old maintenance layer beneath it and completes Calibration 2; Evening turns the discovery back into ordinary guest operations while the resort quietly confirms the Manager as its authority source.

morning.title: Day 11 — The Pier That Wasn't There
morning.openingDialogue: At 8:00, the fourth pier is simply there. Guests assume it is a surprise attraction. Staff assume someone else authorized it. The Manager is handed three forms before breakfast.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Handle guest navigation after the fourth pier appears permanently enough to need a name.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: At 8:00 sharp, a fourth pier is attached to the lighthouse shore. It was open sea yesterday. Kronii is staring at it like time has committed fraud. Bae has three markers. IRyS is trying to stay positive. Fauna is checking whether the seabirds seem bothered.

steps.prompt: The guest map refuses to display the new pier until management enters a temporary name.

options.resultDialogue: You type FOURTH PIER. Every resort map updates instantly. Bae squints. 'Boring.' Kronii folds her arms. 'Accurate.' A second sign appears beneath it: FORMERLY NONEXISTENT. Kronii turns to you. 'Less accurate.'

You type DEFINITELY NORMAL PIER. The sign lights up in cheerful blue. IRyS smiles. 'See? Reassuring.' Kronii points at the ocean where the pier did not exist yesterday. 'The adjective is doing violence to the noun.'

Bae types PIER McPIERFACE before anyone can stop her. Every map updates. Taxi screens update. A lighthouse announcement says, 'Service to Pier McPierface begins at nine.' Kronii grabs Bae. 'UNDO CIVILIZATION.' Bae: 'CIVILIZATION VOTED.'

steps.prompt: The temporary name begins appearing on printed tickets, staff radios, and guest merchandise.

options.resultDialogue: You rename it LIGHTHOUSE PIER 4. The silly merchandise changes mid-print. Bae holds up a shirt reading I VISITED LIGHTHOUSE PIER 4 AND ALL I GOT WAS ADMINISTRATIVE COMPLIANCE. IRyS: 'I'd buy it.' Kronii: 'Do not reward this.'

options.text: Keep the ridiculous name for today
options.resultDialogue: You keep the joke name. Guests immediately start taking photos under the sign. Fauna watches a gull land on it. 'Nature has accepted the branding.' Kronii: 'Nature was not consulted.' Bae bows. 'The market was.'

steps.prompt: The pier is stable, crowded, and somehow already part of the transit map.

options.resultDialogue: You add TEMPORARY ACCESS. The sign accepts the wording. Kronii nods. 'Finally, restraint.' A smaller sign appears: TEMPORARY SINCE 08:00. Bae checks the time. 'Historic landmark.' Kronii walks away.
options.completionDialogue: Promise opened the fourth pier under temporary access rules. The resort map now acknowledges it, even if Kronii does not.

options.text: Open it as a guest promenade
options.resultDialogue: You approve limited public access. IRyS cheers. Fauna establishes a calm walking route. Bae immediately asks about food stalls. Kronii points at the words LIMITED ACCESS. Bae points at the word ACCESS.
options.completionDialogue: Promise opened the fourth pier as a supervised promenade. Guests are delighted by the new view; staff are trying not to discuss where several hundred meters of concrete came from.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: Promise handled the pier's naming crisis. The island now has one more place than it did yesterday and several more opinions.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Stop holoro from creating an international border on a pier connected to the same island.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: Reine has declared that a proper pier requires proper arrivals. Ollie has built a customs booth out of beach umbrellas. Anya is sitting behind the desk with a stamp, half asleep. Every guest entering the pier has come from the resort twenty meters behind them.

steps.prompt: Reine asks what kind of arrival procedure the new pier needs.

options.resultDialogue: You approve a ceremonial stamp. Ollie slams PASSPORT PLEASE onto a sign. The first guest says, 'I came from the hotel.' Ollie leans closer. 'FOREIGN HOTEL.' Reine corrects her. 'Domestic visitor.' Anya stamps the guest's brochure without opening her eyes.
Reine prepares a polished welcome line. The arch above her changes to ROYAL PORT OF ENTRY. She pauses. Ollie salutes. 'YOUR MAJESTY, WE HAVE A BORDER.' Reine: 'We have an arch with delusions.'

Anya receives the stamp. A guest approaches. 'Purpose of visit?' she asks without looking up. 'Walking.' Stamp. 'Duration?' 'Ten minutes.' Stamp. Ollie whispers, 'She is terrifyingly efficient.' Reine: 'She wants to return to sleep.'

steps.prompt: The resort booking system begins treating the pier as a separate destination and asking guests for return tickets.

options.resultDialogue: You write SAME ISLAND — NO PASSPORT REQUIRED. The system accepts it. Ollie starts selling novelty passports instead. Reine inspects one. 'This says Nation of Ollie.' Ollie covers the text. 'Prototype.'

options.text: Turn customs into a comedy attraction
options.resultDialogue: Guests line up to receive absurd entry questions. Anya asks one tourist, 'Are you carrying fruit, weapons, or emotional baggage?' The tourist answers, 'Emotional baggage.' Anya stamps DECLARED. Ollie collapses laughing behind the booth.

steps.prompt: The line is under control. Does the customs booth survive?

options.text: Keep it as a photo booth
options.resultDialogue: You remove every real-looking sign and label it ROLEPLAY ONLY. Reine approves. Ollie adds VERY SERIOUS ROLEPLAY underneath. Anya stamps the label DECLARED.
options.completionDialogue: holoro converted the accidental border into a harmless photo attraction. The pier remains part of the same island despite Ollie's objections.

options.resultDialogue: You dismantle the booth. Ollie stands on the pier side and shouts, 'I SEEK ASYLUM!' Reine walks around the table, takes her by the sleeve, and brings her back. 'Application denied.' Anya carries the stamp away as a pillow.
options.completionDialogue: holoro abolished the island's shortest-lived international border. Ollie has appealed to no recognized authority.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoro welcomed guests to the new pier without successfully creating a sovereign state.

coreActivities.previewDialogue: Keep holoX from claiming unexplained infrastructure as headquarters before anyone has inspected it.
coreActivities.selectedDialogue: La+ stands at the entrance to the fourth pier with her arms crossed. Lui has permits. Iroha has safety tape. Koyori has sample bags. Chloe is wearing sunglasses and pretending the entire pier was holoX's plan.

steps.prompt: La+ announces, 'This unknown pier is clearly a secret holoX facility.' How do you respond?

options.resultDialogue: You approve one folding table. A metal sign rises from the pier: HOLOX FORWARD OPERATING BASE. Lui looks at your tiny table, then the permanent sign. 'Manager approved furniture. The island approved propaganda.' La+ points upward. 'Correct priority.'

Iroha places safety tape across the entrance. The pier generates a second tape line exactly parallel to hers. She nods respectfully. 'It understands perimeter discipline.' Koyori reaches over both lines. Two more lines appear around her. Lui: 'It understands Koyori specifically.'

options.text: Let Koyori request a research zone
options.resultDialogue: Koyori says, 'A small lab area would be efficient.' A clean workbench rises from the deck. Everyone freezes. Chloe leans on it. 'Nice.' Koyori's eyes become dangerous. Lui grabs her shoulders before she can say 'full laboratory.'

steps.prompt: The pier keeps interpreting holoX logistics requests as physical modifications.

options.resultDialogue: Lui writes: one table, four chairs, one barrier. Exactly those items appear. La+ writes THRONE underneath. Nothing happens. She writes it larger. Still nothing. Lui smiles. 'Authorization hierarchy.' La+: 'Treason hierarchy.'

Chloe says, 'Make it less obvious.' Every tourist map removes the pier. The physical pier remains packed with tourists. Koyori stares at the map. 'We have invented classified overcrowding.' Chloe pulls her sunglasses down. 'Perfect.' Lui: 'Undo it.'

steps.prompt: The public area is stable. holoX must leave the unexplored underside alone until noon inspection.

options.resultDialogue: Iroha secures the table and barriers. La+ puts a tiny flag on the table. Lui removes it. La+ puts another. Lui removes that. Chloe quietly starts selling souvenir flags to tourists.
options.completionDialogue: holoX secured the public pier and postponed deeper inspection until the proper team arrives. La+ continues referring to it as 'our mysterious territory.'

options.resultDialogue: You keep Koyori's small workbench under Lui's supervision. Koyori signs the log. The bench prints MANAGER-AUTHORIZED STATION. Lui reads it and looks toward you. 'The wording keeps getting more specific.'
options.completionDialogue: holoX left a small monitored research station on the pier. The island continues to treat Manager authorization as something worth engraving.

coreActivities.completionDialogue: holoX secured the fourth pier without annexing it. This is an improvement over the first proposal.

noon.title: Day 11 — Under the Fourth Pier
